gap: No result ChatGPT got states a figure that a named reviewer measured on these boards: the two mechkeyfoundry pages carry maker ratings only, and the RTINGS best-list page prints no numbers. The openable named observations are PCWorld's 20% battery drop over three days on Bluetooth (Lofree Flow 2 100) and Digital Trends' Monkeytype result of over 100 WPM against a usual 90 to 95 (Flow 2 84), with both reviewers having to get the VIA file from Lofree before they could remap.
standout_why: Compared against the cited RTINGS best low-profile page (updated 2026-10-09), the cited mechkeyfoundry best-of (2026-10-16) and its three-way comparison (2026-10-17). Mechkeyfoundry's author states the figures are maker ratings and did not test the NuPhy or Lofree; neither page gives latency, noise or height. The RTINGS best-list text gives no scores, latency, travel or noise. But RTINGS, a cited rival, holds the full lab table (latency, dBA, travel, force, height, weight): those values show as Locked to non-members on its Flow 2 and Air75 V3 reviews and its Flow 2 vs Air75 V3 comparison, so the side-by-side lab table this angle promised could not be built from pages I could open. What is new is thin and covers the Flow 2 only: one battery observation, one typing-speed observation, and the VIA setup friction. Tom's Guide's typing-test tables came back as navigation only or 403. No named measurement was opened for the Keychron K3 Max, Keychron K1 Max or Logitech MX Mechanical Mini.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. RTINGS keeps the NuPhy Air75 V3 as its top low-profile pick and added the Lofree Flow 2 as the alternative on 2026-03-31; its Flow 2 review says 'excellent for programming' with the caveat of 'somewhat loud typing noise' on the tactile switch. So for a coder in a shared room, the Flow 2 rows to favour are Surfer linear or Void silent, not Pulse tactile. The remapping caveat matters for programming: PCWorld and Digital Trends each had to obtain the VIA JSON from Lofree, and Digital Trends found the Fn key cannot be remapped, so the Flow 2 wins on typing feel and build, not on remapping. The measured-latency and noise comparison that could decide Air75 V3 against Flow 2 stays unsourced.

findings.label: Battery drain in use, observed by PCWorld (Mattias Inghe)
findings.value: 20% of charge over a three-day test, on Bluetooth
findings.note: Published 2026-09-23, tested August 2026, translated from PC för Alla. Unit was the Flow 2 100, Nordic layout, with a 'Silent Edition' sticker; the spec sheet lists Kailh Void while the text calls the switches 'linear Pom Cloud'. The battery level is readable only over Bluetooth, not on the 2.4 GHz adapter. It is the 100-key board (same 3,000 mAh as the 84), backlight state not given, so do not extrapolate to hours. Rated 3 out of 5.

findings.label: VIA remapping setup, observed by PCWorld (Mattias Inghe)

findings.note: Also observed: ships in the Mac/iPad/iPhone profile, switches to Windows/Android by a key shortcut; extra Windows keycaps are in the box but no keycap puller; 'even a heavy keystroke produces only minimal clatter' on the silent unit (no dB figure).
